query: I stopped by the community garden on my walk home today, and the raised beds are absolutely bursting right now—there are plump cherry tomatoes turning deep ruby red right on the vine, fuzzy little squash peeking out under broad, prickly leaves, and the lavender row is so fragrant I could smell it from half a block away. The regular group of retired folks who tend the plots were passing around a jar of homemade lemonade when I passed, and they pressed a cold cup into my hands before I could even say hello, gushing that they’d stirred in a handful of fresh mint they’d harvested that morning. I ended up lingering for almost 40 minutes listening to them trade stories about the weirdest weather they’ve gardened through, from random summer hailstorms to that one April a few years back that hit 90 degrees out of nowhere and made all the tulips bloom and wilt in three days flat. On the makeup remover front, I’ve only ever used products that are cruelty free, and I never go for options that cost a crazy amount, sticking only to picks with a reasonable price tag. I’ve heard the ones that have that nice, super hydrating ingredient everyone raves about for keeping skin soft after taking off makeup work really well.
